paragraphs.text: EVAGRIUS: THE DEBATE ON THE LAW BETWEEN SIMON THE JEW AND THEOPHILUS THE CHRISTIAN.
THE DEBATE ON THE LAW BETWEEN SIMON THE JEW AND THEOPHILUS THE CHRISTIAN.

Evagrius sends greetings to his lord and brother Valerius. I will report to you a most welcome debate that recently took place before our eyes, and I think you too will be glad of it once you know it. It was a debate on the Law between a certain Simon, a Jew, and Theophilus, a Christian.

The Jew spoke as follows: "You cross-worshipper, you standard-bearer, you claim to be a teacher of the Christian law. You have in me a patient listener, provided that you answer my questions and prove the truth, not with seductive speech or clever words, but with the plain evidence of the Law. Either you will refute me today and make me a Christian, or I will defeat you, Nazarene, and make you a Jew."
Theophilus the Christian said: "Let the hunchback not boast as though he stood straight."
Simon the Jew said: "Whom do you worship?"
Theophilus the Christian said: "God."
Simon the Jew said: "My dispute with you is about the crucified Christ, whom you call Lord."
Theophilus the Christian said: "We certainly say so, and we boldly prove that he is Lord and God."

Simon the Jew said: "The voice of the sacred and venerable book of Deuteronomy rings out: 'See that I am, and there is no other god besides me.' Isaiah says: 'I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no god.'"

Theophilus the Christian said: "That is the most sacred voice of Christ. If you want to understand it, you must first believe, and only then will you be able to understand. For Isaiah rebukes you when he says: 'Unless you believe, you will not understand.' Without any doubt, then, we know, recognize and worship God almighty, invisible, immeasurable and incomprehensible, and next we confess Christ as God and the Son of God. And the words 'I am the first and I am the last' signify the two comings of Christ."
Simon the Jew said: "What about the words 'Besides me there is no god'?"

Theophilus the Christian said: "Christ, God and Son of God, said this of himself, because he foresaw that the Antichrist would come and call himself god. The prophet Zechariah speaks of him: 'Behold, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not take note of what is failing, will not seek what is scattered, will not save what is crushed, and will not make whole what is sound; he will devour the flesh of the chosen and overturn their heels. And their sword is upon his arm and upon his right eye. His arm shall wither completely, and his right eye shall be utterly blinded.' Therefore Christ says: 'I am the first and the last, and besides me there is no god.'"
Simon the Jew said: "So you are making two gods?"

Theophilus the Christian said: "God is one, from whom is Christ and in whom is God. So it was with Abraham at the oak of Mamre: three appeared to him, and running to meet them he greeted one, saying: 'Lord, if I have found favor before you, I will take water, and let your feet be washed, and refresh yourselves under the tree.' Three, that is, were seen, and this came from divine foreknowledge, because the tree of Christ's cross would give believers a refreshing shelter. Likewise the prophet says in Psalm 81: 'God stood in the assembly of the gods, and in their midst he judges the gods.' He is surely speaking of Christ, who taught in your synagogues and did great works of power. Then in Psalm 44 he says: 'Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of equity. You have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.' What God, or whom, did he call God, Jew? Surely God the Father is speaking of Christ his Son. On his behalf and about him Jeremiah, the most accepted of the prophets, says: 'This is our God, and there is no other, nor shall any other be reckoned beside him. He found out the whole way of understanding and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved. Afterward he was seen on earth and lived among men.' Again in Psalm 45 he says: 'Be still and see that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted on the earth.' And in Psalm 67: 'Sing to the Lord, sing praise to his name, make a way for him who rises over the west; the Lord is his name.' It would take too long to go through more examples; these few prove the truth."

Simon the Jew said: "These testimonies pile up well enough, sharing one spirit and agreeing with your purpose. But I want you to explain this to me: is there any place where God himself establishes Christ as God? Then at last I will consider believing that Christ is God and the Son of God."

Theophilus the Christian said: "Unbelieving Jew, are you now disputing even about the prophets? Still, here is the answer to your question. God speaks to Moses, saying: 'Behold, I have made you a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.' Notice that this Moses was a type of Christ and was a god to unbelieving nations. How much more is Christ the God of those who believe! Just as Moses freed the people from Egypt, from Pharaoh's harsh slavery, so Christ has freed his people from slavery to idols and from the power of the devil."

Simon the Jew said: "If Christ is God and the Son of God, why is it written in Genesis: 'In the beginning God made heaven and earth'? He could surely have said: 'In the beginning God the Father and God the Son made heaven and earth.'"

Theophilus the Christian said: "You are mistaken, Jew, and you will never find the truth unless you understand the origin of truth. If you are willing to believe, you will also be able to find its beginning, which is Christ, the Son of God. For this is how he says, 'In the beginning God made heaven and earth': that is, by Christ's judgment and according to his will, and after his image and likeness God deigned to make man. For he says: 'Let us make man after our image and likeness!' And again, a little further on, he says: 'God made man after the image of God; male and female he made them.'"
Simon the Jew said: "He could have said this to the angels."

Theophilus the Christian said: "You are mistaken, Jew. To which of the angels did God ever say: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you'? And again he says in a psalm: 'I will make him prince, high above all the kings of the earth.' And he commands the angels to worship Christ. Again in the Song of Deuteronomy he says: 'Rejoice, you nations, with him, and let all the angels of God worship him.'"
Simon the Jew said: "Prove to me that Christ is a prince."

Theophilus the Christian said: "I have already done so. Now take another proof, if even so you are able to believe. When Joshua son of Nun was standing across the Jordan, he saw a man standing there with a two-edged sword in his hand. Joshua said to him: 'Are you for us or for our enemies?' And he answered: 'I am the commander of the army of the majesty of the Lord.'"

Simon the Jew said: "Then I want you to explain to me in what way Christ is the Son of God. For all the saints too have been called sons of God. So, just as you have proved to me that he is a prince, prove to me now that he is the Son of God, born of God. For divinity is far removed from human intercourse and does not mingle in embraces."

Theophilus the Christian said: "You speak like a Jew. For Christ is God, the Son of God, the firstborn, brought forth by the Word, uttered from the mouth, cast forth from an undefiled womb. Just as in the beginning, when God made man from the mud of the earth, he breathed his breath into him and man became a living soul, so too he begot his Word, that is, Christ, from the womb of his heart. As it says in the second book of Kingdoms: 'And the word of the Lord came to the prophet Nathan, saying: Go and say to my servant David: You shall not build me a house to dwell in; but when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish his throne for ever, and I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me, and his house shall be made sure.' Again in Psalm 2 he says: 'Why did the nations rage and the peoples plot vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the peoples gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ: Let us burst their bonds and cast their yoke from us. He who dwells in heaven will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them. Then he will speak to them in his anger and terrify them in his fury. But I have been set by him as king over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming the decree of the Lord. The Lord said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession. You will rule them with a rod of iron and shatter them like a potter's vessel.' Again in Psalm 44: 'My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak my works to the king.' And Isaiah says: 'I have heard of things completed and cut short, for God will make a shortened word in all the earth.' This is the Word that healed our wounds, of which it says in Psalm 106: 'He sent his word and healed them.' Again in another psalm God bears witness through the prophet that he made the heaven we spoke of above from Christ and in Christ, who is the Word of God: 'By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their power by the breath of his mouth.' This is the Word that swiftly ran through the world and turned the souls of the wandering to the Lord through the new law, of which it says in Psalm 147: 'He sends his word to the earth; his word runs swiftly.' And Isaiah says: 'Behold, the word of the Lord has become a curse to them, and they did not want it.' And if you are willing to hear our John, crying out with a prophetic voice: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made.' And again, the Son in the same way bears witness to the Father and testifies to the beginnings of his birth, saying in Solomon: 'I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before all creation. I caused an unfailing light to rise in the heavens. I dwelt on high, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.' You see then, Simon, that when your fathers came out of Egypt it was Christ who went before them in the pillar of cloud. Again, there in the Proverbs of the same author: 'The Lord created me at the beginning of his ways, in the beginning, for his works, before he made the earth and before he established the depths; and before all the hills he begot me. When he prepared the heavens I was there with him, and when he set apart his seat, when he made strong the foundations of the earth, I was with him, setting things in order. I was the one in whom he delighted, and daily I rejoiced before his face, when he rejoiced in the completed world.'"
Simon the Jew said: "He may have said this of Wisdom."

Theophilus the Christian said: "You are mistaken, Jew, and your mind is covered with a veil of ignorance. Not without reason did the most holy Moses cover his face with a veil, the veil that has covered your hearts. So come to the Lord and believe that Christ is God and the Son of God, and the covering of ignorance will be taken from your mind. You think this was said of Wisdom; you do not know that Christ is himself the power of God and the wisdom of God. Indeed, your kings, who reigned by succession, could not receive wisdom and power unless they were called by the name of Christ, that is, the Anointed. I will give Daniel as authority for this, who says: 'Vision and prophet will be sealed, everlasting righteousness will arise, and the Holy of Holies will be anointed. And you will know and understand, from the going forth of the word to answer and to build Jerusalem, until Christ the king.' When Christ came from God, the Christ of Christs, the Lord of lords and the King of your kings, the anointing of Samaria ceased, as did that horn with which your kings were anointed, and all the prophets fell silent, because the one of whom they spoke had come, as Isaiah says: 'I am the one who spoke, and I have come to bring good news.' Therefore, as we have said, he is the Christ of Christs and the Lord of lords. I will give Isaiah as authority, who says: 'The Lord says to my Christ, the Lord, whose right hand I have held, that the nations may heed him: I will break the strength of kings, I will open bronze gates before him, and cities shall not be shut; I will open bronze gates and break iron bars, and I will give you hidden treasures.' Whose right hand, then, did the Father hold, if not that of Christ his Son, whom all the nations have heeded, as he says in a psalm: 'You are always with me; you have held my right hand'? Or what city has been shut against him? And to whom do all the bronze gates lie open, that is, the hearts of each person unlocked by faith in Christ, who by his teaching unlocked the minds and hearts of each? Or will you dare to dispute even his birth, when the same prophet says: 'The word of the Lord came to Ahaz, saying: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depths or on high. And Ahaz said: I will not ask, nor will I put the Lord to the test. And he said: Hear now, house of David: is it a small contest for you to contend with men, that you will now contend with God? Therefore the Lord will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel,' which means 'God with us'?"

Simon the Jew said: "I believe the prophets, and I accept Isaiah above all as fully authoritative. But I think he said this of another virgin. When Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, sent his general to Jerusalem to taunt the living God, Isaiah then prophesied against King Shalmaneser, saying: 'The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.' When the angel struck down one hundred and eighty thousand in the camp of the Assyrians, in that was 'God with us.'"

Theophilus the Christian said: "You are mistaken, Jew, and still you do not put away your unbelief. If you say the daughter of Zion is the virgin, what son did she bear? Who ate butter and honey? Or what infant was it who, before he knew his father or mother, carried off the spoils of Samaria? Or what son of David's line did she have? For Isaiah says: 'Behold, a virgin shall receive in the womb and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel. He shall eat butter and honey; and before the boy knows how to call his father or mother, he will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria against the king of the Assyrians.'"
Simon the Jew said: "Then explain to me how these things stand, so that I may be able to believe: what is meant by the honey and the butter, or what spoils of Samaria Christ took."

Theophilus the Christian said: "If you put away your unbelief, you will hear the truth; otherwise what is written in the psalm may be fulfilled in you: 'Like the deaf asp that stops its ears, which will not hear the voices of the charmers.' Isaiah too cries out boldly against your unbelief, saying: 'The words of this book will be to you like the words of a sealed book: if you give it to someone who knows letters to read, he says, "I cannot read it, for it is sealed." Or if this book is given to someone who does not know letters, and you say, "Read," he says, "I have not learned."' First, then, Christ, like all infants at birth, ate butter and honey; this we believe, and so we keep our faith, as also that he was circumcised on the eighth day. But the butter is understood as the anointing of the Spirit, and the honey is the sweetness of his teaching, which we attain and so arrive at faith. And he carried off the spoils of Samaria in this way: when he was an infant he received gifts from the Magi, gold, frankincense and myrrh; and later, when as a grown man he taught and revealed the whole truth of God, Samaria and
Damascus abandoned their idols and truly believed, forsaking the Assyrian, that is, the devil."

Simon the Jew said: "You are indeed opening up the mysteries well at every point in answer to my questions. But since you have proved that Christ is God, the Son of God, uttered from the mouth of God, begotten by the Word, and born of a virgin, how then do you maintain that he was born of the seed of David in the town of Bethlehem?"

Theophilus the Christian said: "I will give Isaiah as authority, who says: 'A shoot shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from his root, and the Spirit of God shall rest upon him.' The shoot was the Virgin Mary, who came from the seed of David, and from her Christ, the flower of the patriarchs, is born according to the flesh. For God, who in Numbers worked a sign so that a donkey spoke, willed to work a far greater sign, so that Christ would be born of a virgin. Otherwise, what dispute would there be between you and me, if a virgin had not given birth?"
Simon the Jew said: "I believe that a virgin, as you say, conceives by the Spirit. The question is whether a virgin could give birth."

Theophilus the Christian said: "Unbeliever, God was able to split a rock and bring forth water in abundance; how much more was God able to command a virgin to give birth! And I bring you yet another witness, if only you will believe: Baruch son of Neriah, who prophesied in Babylon."

Simon the Jew said: "Do you think me so faithless that I would not accept Baruch, the disciple of Jeremiah, who was sent so often by Jeremiah to address the people, and whom Jeremiah instructed to write down his prophecy? And because Jeremiah knew he would prophesy, it was Baruch who led the people after Jeremiah during the captivity and who prophesied; but he made no mention of Christ."

Theophilus the Christian said: "Then how is it that near the end of his book he prophesied about his birth, the manner of his clothing, his passion and his resurrection, saying: 'This is my anointed, my chosen one, cast forth from an undefiled womb,' and he is said to be born and to suffer? He also foretold his tunic, woven in one piece from the top. All these things, Simon, if you believe in this way, you will recognize as fulfilled when you come to the fullness of our Gospels. And as for his being born in Bethlehem, hear Micah, the prophet of God, saying: 'And you, Bethlehem of Judah, house of Ephrathah, you shall not be too small to be set among the thousands of Judah. For from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, and his possession is from the beginning and from the days of old.'"

Simon the Jew said: "We read much, but we do not understand it in this way. So I want to learn, point by point on each matter I ask you, the proven testimonies of the truth. Furthermore, since God commanded that circumcision be practiced, which he first handed down to the patriarch Abraham, and which you admitted above that Christ underwent, how can you persuade me to believe, when you forbid circumcision?"

Theophilus the Christian said: We forbid circumcising the flesh, but we gladly welcome the circumcised to believe. For Abraham, we believe, became the friend of God through faith before he was circumcised, and he obtained righteousness through faith, not through circumcision. For Scripture says: "For I have made you the father of many nations before the Lord, in whom you believed." And again it says: "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness." He heard this before he was circumcised, and afterward he received circumcision. This showed that two peoples would come to faith in Christ, one from the circumcision and one from the uncircumcision. For if Christ had not been circumcised, how would you believe me today, or the prophets, that he would come from the seed of David? Circumcision is a sign of race, not of salvation.

Simon the Jew said: Then how is it that, when the son of Moses was uncircumcised, the angel would have choked him if Zipporah his mother had not taken a stone and circumcised the boy? And when the blood was flowing, she prayed, saying: "Let the blood of the boy's circumcision stop."

Theophilus the Christian said: You are speaking against yourself, Jew. I showed you earlier how Moses was a type of Christ, and how everything he did went before as an image of Christ. The woman Zipporah, who circumcised the boy, is understood to be the synagogue. And when she says, "Let the blood of the boy's circumcision stop," this means that at the coming of Christ the circumcision of boys came to a stop. Indeed, God says this to Moses: "Build me an altar of uncircumcised stones, and you shall not lay iron upon them." This meant, of course, that Christ at his coming was to build the church from an uncircumcised people.
Simon the Jew said: Prove to me that Christ circumcised no one.

Theophilus the Christian said: Believe, and you will prove it to yourself once you begin to unroll the gospels in their fullness. There you will find Matthew, the apostle who came from the tax collectors, and Zacchaeus, the chief of the tax collectors, and you will find many uncircumcised people who believed along with the Jews. The sacrifices and offerings of bulls and goats and rams and lambs were offered when they were commanded, and they were done away with when they were forbidden. The younger people, that is, ours, was preferred to the elder people, and the new covenant was set above the old. In the same way God commanded that circumcision now be celebrated not in the flesh but in the heart. For God says to Rebecca in Genesis: "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be divided from your belly; one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger." And in Deuteronomy he says: "You nations shall be the head, but the unbelieving people shall be the tail." And when Jacob blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, he crossed his hands and laid his right hand on the younger, and so showed the change in the created order. Concerning the new covenant Isaiah says: "Behold, I make new things, which now spring forth, and I will put rivers in the desert," that is, the gospels in the church. And Jeremiah says: "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will accomplish a new covenant for the house of Israel and the house of Judah, not such a covenant as I made with your fathers on the day when I led them out of the land of Egypt." Now hear about circumcision! Moses the lawgiver says: "In the last days God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, so that you may love the Lord your God." And Jeremiah says: "Men of Judah, and you who dwell in Jerusalem, renew newness among yourselves, and do not sow among thorns. Circumcise yourselves to your God, and circumcise the foreskin of your heart, lest my wrath go forth and burn, and there be no one to quench it." To Jesus son of Nave God said: "Make yourself knives of stone, very sharp, and sit down a second time and circumcise the sons of Israel." Was there no iron at that time? But God was speaking to our Jesus Christ, who through his apostle would circumcise hearts spiritually. That is why our apostle was called Simon and afterward received the name Peter.
Simon the Jew said: You have indeed shown me clear proof from the Scriptures. But what can circumcision of the heart be? Or what foreskin must be cut away from the heart?

Theophilus the Christian said: Every lustful desire is conceived in the heart. So the circumcision of the new covenant is the one that God Christ, the Son of God, showed us: that we cut away from ourselves lust, avarice, malice, greed, thefts, frauds and fornication, and that whatever you do not want done to yourself, you do not do to another. This is the circumcision of Christians. The first of the saints had it too, namely Enoch, Noah, Job and Melchizedek, who had circumcision not of the flesh but of the heart. And God could have formed Adam circumcised if he had wished.

Simon the Jew said: My mind is deeply troubled that Christ could have endured so accursed and shameful a passion, if what you say is really true, that he was fastened by our fathers to the gibbet of the cross. We know well that Haman was crucified by our fathers as one accursed, as he deserved, because he had sought the destruction of our race. Every year when the anniversary comes round we rejoice in his death and celebrate the solemn rites of our vows, as we have received it handed down from our fathers. And we read that Absalom, who was a parricide set on murdering his father, hung on a tree. But if Christ endured the gibbet of this death and hung on a cross, why have we not received this very thing from our fathers [?], and why do we not find his suffering in our Scriptures, so that, if he was an enemy of our nation, we might rejoice? You may well blush, Theophilus, if you cannot prove this claim. For it is written in Deuteronomy: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree."

Theophilus the Christian said: First, take the reasoning behind this saying, and recall the reading from Deuteronomy given above. Of whom was it said? For Moses speaks thus: If anyone has sinned so as to deserve the sentence of death, he shall be punished, and you shall hang him on a tree, and everyone who hangs on a tree shall be accursed. But he said this of the sinner who has committed a mortal sin. Christ, however, had no sin, as all the prophets testify. Yet he had to suffer, so that the scriptures might be fulfilled. For Isaiah says: For he committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, but the Lord handed him over for our sins. And we have shown that the prophet said elsewhere: Behold, the word of the Lord has become a curse to them, and they would not have it. And again he says: He was counted among the accursed. Hear also Jeremiah in the Lamentation over Jerusalem, saying: Christ the Lord was taken in their destruction, under whose shadow we live among the nations. Now we know that the most holy David rested in peace, full of years, and endured no suffering of death or of the cross. Hear, then, Christ speaking in Psalm 21: They have dug through my hands and my feet; they have counted all my bones. They themselves looked and stared at me; they divided my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots. But you, Lord, do not keep your help far off; look to my defence; deliver my soul from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog; save me from the mouth of the lion, and my lowliness from the horns of the unicorns! I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the church I will praise you. Likewise in Isaiah: I have stretched out my hands to a people that does not believe but contradicts me, who walked in ways that were not good but followed after their sins. Likewise in Jeremiah: Come, let us put wood into his bread, and root out his life from the earth. Likewise in Deuteronomy: And your life shall hang before your eyes, and you shall fear day and night, and you shall have no assurance of your life. Likewise in Psalm 118: Pierce my flesh with nails out of fear of you. Likewise in Psalm 140: Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight, and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice. Likewise in Zechariah: And they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced. Likewise in Psalm 87: And I cried to you, Lord; all day long I stretched out my hands to you. Likewise in Numbers: Now God is hanged as a man, and as a son of man he suffers threats. And in the Song of Songs it says in the person of the church: My brother is white and ruddy, and pierced with a lance by the soldiers. As for the whiteness, what else did it show but the faith of the people? The ruddiness, on the other hand, signifies the passion. For this is why he came in his first coming: to display every humiliation and disfigurement, even to the death of the cross. Hear, finally, in Psalm 21: But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach of men and the outcast of the people; all who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and wagged their heads. Likewise in the same place: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue has stuck to my throat, and you have brought me down into the dust of death. Likewise in Psalm 68: It will please the Lord more than a young calf that puts forth horns and hooves. What do you say, Jew? Was David horned? Come now, understand that cluster of grapes in Numbers which two men carried back on a pole from the land of promise. It was surely a figure of Christ hanging on the wood, coming from the land of promise, that is, from Mary, who was of earth-born stock. And the two carrying the pole showed a figure of the two peoples: the one in front, namely yours, turning its back on Christ; the other, behind, looking at the cluster, by which our people is understood.
Simon the Jew said: What will you say about the pomegranate that was brought to Moses together with that same cluster? [?]

Theophilus the Christian said: Quite rightly did the pomegranate follow the cluster. It was, of course, a figure of the church, which holds within itself a people enrolled by the red of Christ's blood.

Simon the Jew said: What will you say about the figs? Or by what arguments in your discourses will you prove that the fig is not sin, since, when Adam, the first-formed man, in his transgression covered his private parts with fig leaves, these represented the itch and bitterness of sin?

Theophilus the Christian said: You understand these things only skin-deep, Jew. For the fig tree and the covering of leaves are understood as a figure of the old man. But if you wish to consider the spiritual man, that is, the inner man, you will find that the fruit of the figs brought to Moses from the land of promise is spiritual life; just as Hezekiah, king of Judea, after his life had been lengthened, received a lump of figs as his chief medicine for the healing of his flesh. For it would have been enough for God to say: I have added fifteen years to the span of your life. But he adds: Take a lump of figs, crush it and apply it as a poultice, and you will be healed; meaning, that once the onrush of lust is broken, you may recover your health. Let us now return to the humility of Christ's first coming, which we were discussing. Hear the prophet Isaiah: God, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We have announced concerning him: like a little child; he has no form nor honour. And we saw him, and he had no form nor beauty: a man set among stripes, and knowing how to bear infirmity. Because his face was turned away, he was despised and not esteemed. He bore our sins and is in sorrows for our sake. And he, because he was ill-treated, was led like a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before its shearer, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. But who will declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth; by the crimes of my people he was led to death. And I will give the wicked in return for his burial and the rich in return for his death, for he committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth. But the Lord handed him over for our sins, and he was counted among the wicked. Likewise in the same place he testifies of the humility of his first coming, saying: I gave my back to the scourges and my cheeks to the slaps, and I did not turn my face away from the filth of spitting, and the Lord was my helper. And Jeremiah says: I was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and I did not know it. It was with this lamb, as an image of Christ, that Moses celebrated the Passover in Egypt at the deliverance of the people. Nor could the people have been freed from the house of bondage or from the oppression of Pharaoh unless the lamb was slain and the Passover celebrated and the doorposts of the houses marked with its blood, so that when the destroying angel came and saw the sign of the blood, those who were in the houses might be saved. This mystery, foretold beforehand, was fulfilled in the coming of Christ. For this is why Christ was slain in his first coming: to free us from the power of the devil and from the worship of idols. And he is called a yearling because, after he was dipped in the Jordan, he preached for one year and then suffered; and with his blood we are marked on the forehead, so that at the second coming, when the destruction of this world comes, we may be saved. As my authority for this I will cite the prophet Ezekiel, who himself also signifies the two comings of Christ, saying: Go through the midst of Jerusalem and mark a sign on the foreheads of the men who grieve and groan over the iniquities that are done in the land. And again he signifies the second coming, the destruction of those not marked, saying: Go into the city and do not spare old or young; kill women and little children with the sword, so that they may be wiped out; but do not touch those on whom you find the sign, and begin from my holy ones. This sign Rahab the harlot also, who was a figure of the church, hung in her window, a scarlet cord, so that when Joshua came to conquer Jericho, on seeing the sign of the scarlet, Rahab and those who were in her house might be saved. So too at the coming of Christ, when Christ the Son of God comes to burn up this world with fire, the church and those who are found in it marked on the forehead will be saved; just as Hosea, who was a type of Christ, is commanded to take a wife of fornication, that is, the church, which Christ took out of the fornication of idols: The Lord said this: Take to yourself a wife of fornication; that is, he took her out of the fornication of idols, since the service of idols is the beginning of fornication.

Simon the Jew said: So the church is a harlot? Theophilus the Christian said: What does "harlot" mean but one who gives herself to all who come? So too the church refuses to none who come to her the gain of faith. For having repudiated the synagogue, Christ took the church to himself. Hear Jeremiah saying: I have put away your mother and given her a bill of divorce; for I gave it to your mother, because I put her away. And another prophet says: Plead with your mother, for I am not her husband. For this is Christ the Son of God, the righteous one, of whom Solomon too prophesied in the person of the Jews, saying: Let us therefore lie in wait for the righteous one, for he is of no use to us and is opposed to our works; he reproaches us with sins against the law and denounces us for sins against our training; he claims to have knowledge of God and calls himself the Son of God. And he has become to us a reproof of our thoughts. He is grievous to us even to behold, for his life is unlike that of others, and his ways are different. We are counted by him as triflers, and he keeps himself from our ways as from uncleanness; he extols the latter end of the righteous and boasts that he has God for his father and calls himself the Son of God. Let us see, then, whether his words are true, and let us test what will happen to him, and let us learn what his end will be. For if he is truly the Son of God, God will take him up and deliver him from the hands of his adversaries. Let us examine him with insult and torture, that we may learn his reverence and prove his patience. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death; for, by his own words, he will be looked after. These things they thought, and they went astray; for their own malice blinded them, and they did not know the mysteries of God. And Moses says in Deuteronomy: You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous. That he rose from the dead the scriptures testify. We find in Psalm 15: For you will not abandon my soul to hell, nor will you let your holy one see corruption. You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with your countenance. Likewise in Psalm 29: Lord, you have brought my soul up from the underworld. Likewise in Psalm 3 he says: I lay down and slept, and I rose up, for the Lord will sustain me. And the prophet Hosea testifies that he rose from the dead on the third day, saying: He will revive us after two days, on the third day. Likewise the Lord says to Moses in Exodus: Go down and charge the people, and purify them today and tomorrow, that they may wash their garments and be ready on the third day. For it was on the third day that the Lord appeared on Mount Sinai. And Jonah, when he was sent to preach to the Ninevites, displayed a type of Christ, who after three days was to come out of the belly of the whale, which was hell. And Isaiah says: Now I will arise, says the Lord; now I will be glorified; now you will see; now you will be ashamed. Vain will be the strength of your hope; fire will consume you. And in Psalm 77 he says: And the Lord arose as one asleep, and like a mighty man flushed with wine. In speaking of wine, his passion is indicated. For during his passion there was darkness from the sixth hour until the ninth hour; night shut out the day, as the prophet Amos says: The sun shall set at noon, and the day of light shall be darkened, and I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. And Jeremiah says: She who gives birth is terrified; her soul is weary; the sun has set while it is still day; she is confounded and accursed; the rest of them I will give to the sword in the sight of their enemies. And that after the resurrection he ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father, all the scriptures testify, saying in Psalm 67: Make a way for him who ascends above the setting of the sun; the Lord is his name. They will be troubled at his presence, the father of orphans and judge of widows. Likewise in Psalm 46: God has gone up with jubilation, and the Lord with the sound of the trumpet. Likewise in Psalm 18: His going forth is from the height of heaven, and his circuit to the height of heaven, and there is none who can hide from his heat. The law of the Lord is spotless, converting souls. Likewise in Psalm 17: He bowed the heavens and came down, and darkness was under his feet; and he mounted upon the Cherubim and flew; he flew upon the wings of the winds, and made darkness his hiding place; at the brightness before him the clouds passed by, hail and coals of fire; and the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave forth his voice; he sent from on high and took me and delivered me and rescued me from my most powerful enemies and from those who hated me. And Isaiah says: Who is this who comes from Edom, the Lord, with garments red from Bozrah, so glorious in his robe and mighty? And in the person of Christ the answer is given: I argue judgment and proclaim the truth. Likewise in Psalm 23, as Christ ascended into heaven, it was said to the angels who keep the gates: Lift up your gates, you princes, and be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory shall come in. But they, who knew that Christ had been introduced into the virgin by the Word, marvelling that he was ascending into heaven in such a guise and bringing back a victorious trophy, ask: Who is this King of glory? And they are answered: The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory. Likewise in Psalm 109: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet. The Lord sends forth the rod of your power from Zion; rule in the midst of your enemies. With you is sovereignty in the day of your power, in the splendour of the saints. From the womb, before the morning star, I begot you. The Lord has sworn and will not repent: You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek; the Lord is at your right hand. Hear now also of the glory of the kingdom of his second coming in Daniel: I saw in a vision of the night, and behold, in the clouds of heaven one like a son of man coming; he came up to the Ancient of Days, and royal power was given to him; all the kings of the earth by their nations and all glory shall serve him; and his faith is everlasting, which shall not be moved, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed. Likewise in Psalm 92: The Lord has reigned; he has put on beauty; the Lord has put on strength and girded himself with power. For he has established the world, which shall not be moved. Your throne is prepared, O God; you are from everlasting. And in Psalm 49: The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and has called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting; out of Zion is the beauty of his comeliness. God will come openly, our God, and he will not keep silence. Fire will burn before him, and round about him a mighty tempest. He called the heaven above and the earth, to judge his people. Gather to him his holy ones, those who ordain his covenant with sacrifices. And the heavens will declare his righteousness, for God is judge. Likewise in Psalm 44 he says: Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty, in your comeliness and your beauty; and set forth, proceed prosperously, and reign because of truth and gentleness and righteousness. Likewise in Psalm 95 he says: Say among the nations: The Lord has reigned from the tree. Likewise in Isaiah: A child is born to us, whose government is upon his shoulders, and his name shall be called Angel of Great Counsel. And if you wish to learn the fullness of the gospels, you will find in our John that Christ, going to his passion, carried the cross on his shoulders, which is why Isaiah says: whose government is upon his shoulders. Likewise in Psalm 71: O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son, to judge your people in righteousness and your poor with judgment. Let the mountains receive peace for your people, and the hills righteousness. He will judge the needy of the people and save the children of the poor, and he will humble the false accuser; and he will endure with the sun and before the moon, from generation to generation. In his days righteousness shall spring up, and abundance of peace, until the moon is lifted up. And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth. The Ethiopians shall fall down before him, and his enemies shall lick the dust, and they shall worship him always; all day long they shall bless him. And there shall be a firm support on the earth, on the tops of the mountains; his fruit shall be exalted above Lebanon, and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth. Let his name be blessed for ever and ever; his name endures before the sun, and his throne before the moon; and in him all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed; all nations shall magnify him.

Simon the Jew said: You have indeed shown me, with clear proof from my own scriptures, that all things were prefigured in Christ. And I would indeed have wished to believe, had not the consideration of this psalm held me back. For this psalm was spoken of Solomon; indeed its very title refutes you, since it says: A Psalm for Solomon.

Theophilus the Christian said: That envious one who deceived the first-formed man and has now led your people astray, through whose envy death came into the world, has evidently taken hold of the understanding of your heart too, so that, poor wanderer, you do not understand a matter that is plain and set in full light. For Solomon reigned forty years within the fixed borders of Judea, from Dan to Beersheba, and afterwards he sinned, as it says in the third book of Kingdoms: And Solomon did evil and did not walk in the way of his father David, and he built an idol of Moab, Chemosh, and of Trivia, the abomination of the Sidonians; and the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon himself, Hadad the Edomite. But the kingdom of Christ has been extended beyond unknown wildernesses. For of whom does God say through the prophet: And he will endure with the sun and before the moon, from generation to generation, and he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth? Does he say this of Solomon, whose kingdom and years I showed you above? But Christ reigns always and everywhere.
Simon the Jew said: The devil, the enemy of my fathers, who was blinding the eyes of my heart, is departing from my mind, as I see. For I have begun to desire to recognize the light of truth.

Theophilus the Christian said: Believe, then, so that you, enlightened on every point, may come out of your chains, as Isaiah says of Christ: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; therefore he has anointed me and sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal the broken-hearted, to lead out those bound in chains, and from the prison house those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to give light to the blind. For what is meant by the prison house and men held down in chains but the people of this world, held fast by the blindness of ignorance and chained by the sins of the devil? As it says in Genesis: And darkness was over the abyss, and God said: Let there be light! For what is meant by the abyss but the hearts of men blinded by the darkness of ignorance? But when Christ, who is the light, comes, the darkness of ignorance departs.

Simon the Jew said: You have indeed revealed to me many things hidden and unheard of. But there still remains in my soul a scruple of distrust, because you observe everything religiously, yet you neglect the Sabbath, which God commanded to be kept and observed; and besides, you take food and wine in the manner of the Gentiles, although God specifically prescribed which animals and fish ought to be eaten and which are to be abhorred, and that their carcasses are not to be touched. Unless this too is proven to me from the scriptures, I am afraid to take the risk of believing.

Theophilus the Christian said: I have already told you above that the devil envies you, because you are, of course, the son of your fathers. They were upheld by so many benefits and set free from Egypt, with the sea standing round them in waves like walls; in the desert they were furnished with lavish feasts and filled with the heavenly food of manna; and yet they lapsed into forgetfulness and dared to demand profane gods to worship. Rightly does God rebuke and reproach your race through Jeremiah, saying: “If the Ethiopian will change his color and the leopard his spots, then you too will change from your evil teaching.” The sabbath, of course, was handed down as a figurative rest of the seventh day. This was first because Joshua son of Nun, in order to conquer Jericho, went around the walls once each day for seven days, with men bearing weapons of war and carrying the ark of the covenant; but on the seventh day they went around seven times. It is plainly true that either they began on a sabbath, or they conquered Jericho on a sabbath when its walls fell. There is also the fact that in the Maccabees they won their greatest victory over their enemies on a sabbath and took vengeance on their adversaries with their swords on a sabbath. There is also the fact that God rejects a human sabbath, as Isaiah says: “My soul hates your fasting and your feast days and your sabbaths. You have become a surfeit to me; I will no longer forgive your sins.” But the sabbath God desires is that you rest from wicked works, so that in the seven-thousandth year, which is understood as the sabbath of sabbaths, you may be found clean of evil works. This will be the delightful sabbath, holy to God, in which God takes pleasure. As for the foods you doubt whether you ought to eat: you are forbidden to take in not the flesh of swine, but swinish deeds. Just so, wallowing in water mixed with mud, you join your sister to yourself in marriage, you unite blood with blood, you scour the earth for plunder, you make a public show of your feasts, you pray in the streets. See how you sin! And you do not understand that it is written of you in Psalm 16: “They were filled with swine's flesh and left the remains to their little ones”; that is, you pass your sin on to your posterity. As for fish, you eat those with scaly skin; but the others, which you pretend to avoid, once they are drawn up in the nets and mixed in with the mass of fish and thoroughly pressed out into fish sauce, you eat with relish. Now show me from scripture where you have learned that the wine of Christians is forbidden, and you will rightly be able to defeat me. But I will show you where Jewish wine is forbidden and where we are prohibited from eating your foods. Hear the prophet Isaiah saying: “Your hands are full of blood; wash yourselves, be clean!” Again, in Psalm 13 he says: “Their feet are swift to shed blood. Ruin and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known.” See what feet these are! And with what hands you make your wine and your unleavened bread! And in Deuteronomy he says: “For their wine is from the vine of Sodom, and their vine-shoots from Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall, a cluster of bitterness is in them. Their wine is the rage of dragons and the incurable rage of asps. Are not these things gathered up with me and sealed in my treasuries?”

You have been refuted by so many great testimonies, Simon; if you still cannot believe, you are speaking against your own salvation. Read Daniel, and you will find Nebuchadnezzar saying: “Did we not cast three men into the furnace? Look, I see four men, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of God.” What do you say, Jew? The barbarian Nebuchadnezzar recognized the Son of God, whom you are slow to find. And take care that the reproach of the prophet Habakkuk is not fulfilled in you, when he says: “Look, you scoffers, and see and marvel, for I am doing a work in your days that you will not believe if anyone tells it to you.”

Simon the Jew said: Bearer of salvation, Theophilus, good physician of the sick, I can say no more. Have me instructed as a catechumen and consecrated with the sign of faith in Jesus Christ. For I believe that through the laying on of hands I shall receive the washing away of my sins.

Theophilus the Christian said: Rather, a blessing! So Isaac blessed Jacob, and Jacob received the blessing through the laying on of a hand, so that the greater came from the lesser. So too Ephraim and Manasseh were made great through the laying on of hands.

Then Theophilus anointed Simon the Jew. And having gained faith, Simon began to give thanks, saying: “I thank you, Jesus, whom I have never seen face to face, yet now I believe in you. Thanks be to you, Jesus, whom I never heard, yet now I hear you. I call upon you, Jesus, whom I did not understand before, yet now I long for my understanding to be in you, through whom I have come to know Theophilus your disciple. Lord Jesus, if I am worthy of faith, strengthen me also in the knowledge of you. For you show the way to those who wander, you call back the lost, you raise the dead, you strengthen the faithless with your faith, and you enlighten the eyes of the heart of the blind. You yourself are the holy tabernacle that was with our fathers in the desert; you are the lampstand of light, you the altar and the bread of the Presence, you the altar of sacrifice, you the freewill offering. You, Lord, are life and pearl, crystal, yoke and plough. I pray you, Lord, do not remember my ignorance and unbelief. For you are the giver of hidden blessings, and you have deigned to give me all things. To you be honor, power, praise and glory, here and through all the immortal ages of ages. Amen.”
